source.title: Model Merging is Secretly Certifiable: Non-Vacuous Generalisation Bounds for Low-Shot Learning
source.authors: Taehoon Kim; Henry Gouk; Minyoung Kim; Timothy M. Hospedales

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the paper and supplementary material; no relevant section appears cut off.
record.tranche_reason: Measures actual and certified generalisation gaps for model merging in few-shot image classification, a setting not covered by the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports train/test errors and actual or certified gaps for few-shot model merging. Those results bear on generalisation gaps but do not test V1–V8 as specified. The paper also cites Zhang et al. (2017) and other prior work; those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures empirical and certified generalisation gaps for few-shot model merging, but none of its experiments tests V1–V8. Generalisation certificates and support-set-size effects do not establish any of the specified memorisation, width, architecture, optimiser, batch-size, dropout, sharpness-ranking, or example-removal effects. References to original studies provide background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors demonstrate non-vacuous certificates for model-merging learners with large vision and language models and small support sets. Bound optimisation and data-dependent priors can improve certificates. The Gaussian PAC-Bayes certificates concern stochastic Gibbs predictors; a separate discretised variant certifies deterministic merges. Main results emphasize tasks where the underlying merging learner succeeds.
record.recipe_differences: Studies few-shot model merging and PAC-Bayes certificates, rather than the original studies' interventions or measurements of memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.method_sensitivity: The certified gap changes with training dataset size in the reported Task-wise AdaMerging experiment. The paper also reports that bound optimisation and data-dependent priors affect certification and empirical performance, but those are not mapped to V1–V8.

fits_no_version.finding: For bound-optimised Task-wise AdaMerging of CLIP-ViT-B/32 models, increasing support-set size reduces the certified generalisation gap across five image datasets. The text reports certificates within five percentage points of training error with a few thousand examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing support-set size can tighten PAC-Bayes generalisation certificates for few-shot model merging.

record.problems: The dataset-size gap results are shown only in Figure 4, without exact values in the text. The experiment concerns model merging and certified gaps, not standard gradient training or the specific conditions in V1–V8.
record.rows_left_out: Other train/test error and PAC-Bayes results, including Tables 1–3 and 5–9, concern merging methods, certification objectives, or specific downstream tasks and do not test V1–V8. The paper reports numerous per-method and per-dataset values; they are not extracted because those conditions do not map to the listed versions or provide additional rows for the selected dataset-size finding.

untested.parts: No paired natural-label and random-label training or held-out evaluation.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive optimiser versus SGD comparison under limited or broader tuning.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted training recipes.
No magnitude-aware sharpness ranking of generalisation gaps or comparison with norm and margin measures. Gaussian perturbations of merging coefficients serve certification, not this correlation test.
No identification and removal of memorised examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification should be changed: a new setting qualifies only when its results bear on a listed version. Row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, despite the reported certified-gap trend being supported by the text. Other certification and merging-performance results are already declared in rows_left_out and require no missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fitting random labels alongside generalisation on natural labels.
Does not sweep network width beyond interpolation.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected image classifiers.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD under the version's tuning conditions.
Does not compare large and small batches under fixed epoch budgets.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with other generalization measures.
Does not remove memorized training examples.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-B/32 with Task-wise AdaMerging
rows.stage_stated: few-shot merging; 100 examples per target dataset in the main experiments
rows.operation_detail: Varied training dataset size and reported actual and certified generalisation gaps.
rows.value: Figure only; the text says increasing dataset size shrinks the certified generalisation gap.
rows.locator: Figure 4; supplementary Section 7.2 defines the actual gap as test error minus train error and the certified gap as PAC-Bayes bound minus train error.
rows.note: Exact plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Figure 4 reports EuroSAT results for bound-optimised Task-wise AdaMerging; the condition should explicitly include bound optimisation. The certified-gap trend is stated, but it measures no listed version. Actual and certified gaps are separate measures and should be separate rows if retained.
